extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers and policy analysts studying corporate R&D, innovation, and patent-science linkages
extracted.subtask_short: measuring firm research use in patents
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical procedures and measurement rules for linking corporate scientific publications to patent citations to study how firms invest in research and how that research is used internally versus spilled over to others. Covers sample selection, matching algorithm, variable construction, classification rules, and econometric specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure corporate research by scientific publications authored by researchers employed by firms
rubrics_metrics.description: We measure corporate research by scientific papers authored by researchers employed by firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match sample firms to Web of Science (WoS) using the affiliation field; include articles from journals covered in the 'Science Citation Index' and 'Conference Proceedings Citation Index - Science', excluding social sciences, arts and humanities articles. Identified ~300,000 articles with at least one author employed by sample Compustat firms (1980–2006). See Appendix 6.2 for matching details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure use of research as inputs into inventive activity by patent citations to corporate publications
rubrics_metrics.description: We measure the use of research as inputs into inventive activity by citations in the firm’s patents to its own scientific publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat a citation by a patent to a corporate publication as an indicator that the patented invention used or built upon the knowledge in the publication; distinguish internal citations (same firm) and external citations (other firms). Use front-page non-patent literature (NPL) references matched to WoS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal citation (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal citation is a citation by a patent to a scientific publication produced by the same firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count citations where patent owner and cited publication affiliation map to the same ultimate-owner parent company (UO); aggregate subsidiaries to the UO level so citations across subsidiary/parent are counted as internal.

rubrics_metrics.name: External citation / spillover (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spillovers are measured by citations in the patents of other firms to the focal firm’s scientific publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use external citations to capture public spillovers and analyze their relationship with corporate publication output and private returns; compare effect sizes of internal vs external citations (paper finds one internal citation ~ negative effect of four external citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching NPL citations to WoS publications (algorithmic standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform a many-to-many match between NPL citations and WoS corporate publications using a specialized matching algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match based on standardized authors' names, number of authors listed, article title, journal name and year; algorithm accounts for misspelling, unstructured text, incomplete references, and other issues. Allow more than one publication per citation; perform extensive manual checks (details in Appendix 6.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Select publicly traded U.S. firms with active Compustat records and positive R&D expenses for at least one year during 1980–2006 and at least one patent; exclude firms not headquartered in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final estimation sample: unbalanced panel of 4,736 firms and 57,765 firm-year observations; 2,413 firms have at least one scientific publication during the sample period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate to ultimate-owner-parent-company (UO) level
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate data to the ultimate-owner-parent-company level to handle subsidiaries and complex ownership structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a subsidiary publishes but parent is patent assignee, record both at the UO level so a patent-to-publication citation is considered internal. See Appendix 6.1 for procedures dealing with multiple firm identifiers and ownership changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion / exclusion of publication types in WoS coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Include journals covered in WoS 'Science Citation Index' and 'Conference Proceedings Citation Index - Science'; exclude social sciences, arts and humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WoS covers ~5000 journals; use affiliation field to identify corporate-authored papers; classification to main fields by WoS journal subject category.

rubrics_metrics.name: R&D stock construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute R&D stock using a perpetual inventory method with a 15 percent depreciation rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R&D stock is calculated with Rt as R&D expenditure in year t and delta = 0.15. Patent stock and GRD stock are constructed analogously (see footnote/formulas in text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal lagging of internal citation and publication variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Define internal citation as the lagged number of patent citations to own publications (patents granted up to year t-1 to publications published up to year t-1) when predicting publications in year t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The baseline regression uses ln(1 + Publications_it) on ln(1 + Internal_citation_{i,t-1}) plus lagged controls to mitigate simultaneity and common-shock concerns; other lag structures (2–3 years) are also checked in robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Econometric controls and fixed effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Include firm fixed effects, year dummies, industry fixed effects (where relevant), and lagged firm-year controls (patent stock, R&D stock, sales); include dummy for zero publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These controls are used to mitigate bias from unobserved heterogeneity and scale differences; specifications include pooled, between-firm, and within-firm (fixed effects) estimations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of patent-to-publication citation as measure of use of science
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate NPL-to-WoS citation measure using Carnegie Mellon Survey (CMS) responses on the role of science in corporate R&D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show correlations between average patent citations to science and survey-reported use of public science (CMS Q.18, Q.22); perform regression controls for firm size and backward patent citations and include industry-year dummies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrumental variable strategy using Inevitable Disclosure Doctrine (IDD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use variation across states and over time in the application of the Inevitable Disclosure Doctrine as an instrument for internal use of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: IDD restricts mobility of scientists and inventors, tightening the link between research and development personnel, thereby increasing internal use; conduct mean-comparison tests and IV estimation using state-level effective dates of IDD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify publications as 'recent' (temporal window)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'recent' science as publications published no later than five years from the grant year of the citing patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical heterogeneity tests show internal citations to recent science (<= 5 years) have positive effects, whereas citations to older science do not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify basic vs applied publications using CHI index or JIF
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between citations to basic and applied publications using CHI research categories or Journal Impact Factor (JIF) median.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic journals = top CHI categories or JIF above median; about 70% of internal citations are to basic science and these citations drive future publication output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication quality classification via normalized citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify publication quality by number of citations an article receives divided by the average citations received by all WoS publications published in the same journal-year; high vs low based on median of normalized citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only citations to high-quality publications significantly affect future corporate publication production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define core technology and core vs non-core citing patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the firm's core technology as the IPC (International Patent Classification) with the majority of the firm's patents in a given year; core citations are citations made by patents in that core area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal citations made by core-technology patents have a much stronger relationship with future publications than non-core citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent quality classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure patent quality by forward citations a patent receives divided by average number of citations received by all patents granted in the same year; classify patents as high/low quality by median.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal citation effects on future publications are stronger for citations made by high-quality patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor-author overlap metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the tie between research and development personnel as the share of patents that list at least one scientist (publication author) as an inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a firm-level organizational feature; firms with higher inventor-author overlap have higher internal citation shares and more publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness checks excluding potential confounders (self-citations, examiner-added citations, clinical trials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform robustness checks excluding internal self-citations to own patents, citations added by patent examiners, and clinically-focused trial publications in pharma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results remain robust; coefficient on self-citations is statistically zero; clinical trial publications identified by title/abstract phrases (<100) excluded with no substantive change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Many-to-many matching allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow more than one publication to be matched to each NPL citation (many-to-many match).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied across all patents granted 1980–2014, matching ~14 million citations to ~300k corporate publications; resulting matched set includes 266,361 patent citations to 50,494 corporate publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of log-transformed dependent and main independent variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Model ln(1 + Publications_it) as a function of ln(1 + Internal_citation_{i,t-1}) and controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline econometric specification shown in equation (1); interpretation of coefficients reported (e.g., one additional internal citation associated with ~0.5 publication per firm-year in fixed-effects specification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify high vs low internal citation share firms for comparative tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Define firms with above-mean value share of internal citations as high internal citation firms for mean comparison tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare characteristics (number of publications, R&D intensity, inventor-author overlap) between high- and low-internal-citation firms (Table 3).
